THE COMPOSITION PARADIGM
Not a component library.
A composition system.

A resource catalogue gives you reusable building blocks. Tessellate adds a product brief, shared design settings, and a manifest that connects screens, resources, and project intent.

Starting from a Resource Catalogue
Choose resources: The product team decides which components belong on each screen.
Carry design decisions: Shared tokens and interaction patterns need to stay aligned across resources.
Connect the screens: The team defines navigation, content, and how interface parts work together.
Review generated code: Check markup, styles, and behavior in the context of the product.
Outcome: Resource choice, integration, and consistency remain with the product team.
Tessellate Composition Engine
Product model: Interprets a brief into a product domain, audience, and user jobs before planning screens.
Design DNA: Shared visual settings guide composition and apply to resources that support them.
Manifest audit: A 100-point rubric scores declared structure and resource metadata; it does not certify the rendered interface.
Validated mutations: Workbench and integration tools apply typed manifest changes while respecting locked scope.
Outcome: Export a standalone React + Tailwind project from the manifest you composed and reviewed.

Tessellate rejects arbitrary visual hallucination. Every screen is an Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) governed by canonical schemas.

The 12 Dimensions of Design DNA

Every interface system in Tessellate is defined along 12 continuous normalized axes (0–100):

dataDensity (0–100)
trust (0–100)
interactionDensity (0–100)
visualAmbition (0–100)
motion (0–100)
typographicExpression (0–100)
imageryIntensity (0–100)
depth (0–100)
colorSaturation (0–100)
radiusScale (0–100)
borderWeight (0–100)
contrastFloor (0–100)
Canonical Package Schemas

Import Zod contracts directly into your TypeScript projects:

import {
  ResourceManifestSchema,
  ProjectManifestSchema,
  DesignDNASchema,
  ScreenNodeSchema
} from '@tessellate/schemas';

Project manifests, edits, checkpoints and saved resource collections use browser storage on this origin. Export your project to retain a portable copy. Clearing browser site data removes local records.

Core browsing, composition, editing and export need no provider key. BYO provider credentials must remain ephemeral and are never written to project manifests, D1 or R2.

Hosting

ChatGPT Sites serves the site and receives ordinary page and asset requests. Review the hosting provider privacy policy for its processing. Tessellate does not add third-party analytics, advertise fabricated usage counts or provision an additional database for this review.

Public previews

Resource previews use sandboxed frames without same-origin privileges. Treat all example content as synthetic demonstration data, not real employee records.
